history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: the CSV row 'Rukmini Temple, Solapur' has no clear standalone referent in Solapur city. This file documents the only well-documented standalone Rukmini shrine in Solapur district: the Lakhubai Temple at Dindiravan, Pandharpur, listed on travel directories as 'Shri Lakhubai Temple Rukmini Mandir'. TOWN CORRECTED: Pandharpur (CSV said Solapur; Pandharpur is about 70 km west of Solapur city). COORDINATES APPROXIMATE (town-level; the shrine's exact spot within the Dindiravan area has not been precisely geocoded - verify). Local tradition, recorded by scholar R.C. Dhere, holds that Rukmini, angered at Krishna, withdrew to the Dindiravan forest to perform penance, and Krishna came searching for her; the two reconciled here. Another local legend credits the goddess with slaying the demon Dindirasura, from whom the forest takes its name. The deity is a shapeless sacred stone covered with red lead; a sculpted image behind it resembles Gajalakshmi rather than conventional Rukmini iconography. One directory source credits a stone reconstruction to Dhondbhat Katake in 1780 (verify). The shrine sits on the bank of the Chandrabhaga river, north of Dindiravan, in the Chinch Baag area of Pandharpur.

town_description: Pandharpur is a major pilgrimage town in Solapur district on the crescent-shaped Chandrabhaga (Bhima) river, often called the 'Southern Kashi' of Maharashtra. It is the spiritual heart of the Warkari sect and the home of the famous Shri Vitthal-Rukmini (Vithoba) temple, one of the most visited temples in Maharashtra. Millions of Warkari pilgrims walk to Pandharpur during the Ashadhi and Kartiki Ekadashi yatras, singing abhangas; a dip in the Chandrabhaga is believed to wash away sins.
